{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Co-Development Agreement (Execution Version)

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (for PB / Customer)
**Re:** Playbook review of the SFJ Co-Development Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Execution Version against our playbook. Nine of the eighteen rules are met, several of them comfortably in our favour: PB carries no exclusivity, non-compete or MFN obligation, SFJ has no audit right over PB, there is no auto-renewal or renewal uplift, and PB owns Trial Inventions outright with freely-assignable, multi-tier sublicensable flow-down licences (licence scope sits at or above the fallback).

The problems cluster in three places. First, **ownership of our own data**: Section 11.1.1.4 vests the Trial Data Package — all clinical trial data and Research Results generated under our Development Program — in SFJ until we buy it back. Second, **IP indemnity asymmetry**: SFJ's indemnity says nothing about third-party IP infringement, while PB's indemnity at 12.1.2(f) covers infringement caused by "either Party", so PB carries a one-way IP indemnity that also protects SFJ for SFJ's own conduct. Third, **the exit economics**: Article 14.2 imposes formula-driven termination payments on PB of 100%–300% of Development Costs (plus a 25% interest variant), PB has no workable convenience exit, SFJ may terminate on a Change of Control of PB, and Section 4.2.3(ii) locks us into a $110 million minimum funding election.

Supporting gaps: no liability cap at all (both sides uncapped, no carve-outs), arbitration rather than the Delaware courts that match the Delaware governing law, no SFJ performance warranty (Section 13.6.2 disclaims everything outside Article 13), no general post-exit transition or data-export right, an over-long non-solicit tail, and no SFJ-level E&O or cyber cover.

One item requires attention before we send: the termination-for-convenience redline is marked **needs_review** and failed verification. It should not go out in its current form.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification and Insurance (Art. 12; 12.1.1(a)–(f), 12.1.2(f), 12.2.1) | No SFJ third-party IP indemnity; PB's indemnity covers infringement by "either Party". Adding a reciprocal SFJ IP indemnity with standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x-annual-amounts super-cap (non-zero floor); narrowing 12.1.2(f) to PB's own performance. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | Intellectual Property and PII (§ 11.1.1.4) | SFJ is sole owner of the Trial Data Package until PB buys it back. Flipping ownership to PB, limiting SFJ to processing to perform its obligations, conforming the Exhibit K mechanic; payment consideration and the 14.3.1 backstop assignment left intact. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.2.6; § 15.6 | SFJ may terminate on a PB Change of Control (150% of Development Costs); no-consent carve-out is mutual; competitor bar lapses at Program Transfer. Targeting preferred: PB-only carve-out, reasonableness standard for SFJ, permanent competitor bar, removal of 14.2.6 and its dependent consequences. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | Term and Termination (§§ 14.2.1–14.2.10) | Termination payments of 300% / 150% / 100% of Development Costs, plus Development Costs at 25% annual interest. Revised § 14.2.11 supersedes the Development-Cost formulas with a single fee capped at 3x average monthly Development Costs over the preceding 12 months; Article 6 Approval Payments and Buy-Out Payments preserved. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review (verification failed)** | Term and Termination (§ 14.2.2) | PB's only exit is gated on $60m of Development Costs, closes at first Regulatory Approval and costs 300% of Development Costs. Proposed cure: 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts and a bar on SFJ convenience termination. **Do not circulate pending re-verification.** |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 3.19 (Exclusive Period, § 1.1.68) | Meets preferred: the only exclusivity covenant binds SFJ in PB's favour; no sourcing or sole-supplier obligation on PB. Article 7.5 covenants are financing-style and outside this rule. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | Intellectual Property and PII (§§ 11.1.1.3–11.1.1.4) | Sits at or above the fallback: PB owns Trial Inventions and the flow-down licences are worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable and sublicensable through multiple tiers. "Perpetual/irrevocable" labelling and the commercially-reasonable-efforts procurement obligation noted only. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 3.19; § 15.15 | Meets preferred: no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on PB; Article 7.5 covenants are collateral-protection mechanics with an Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-out. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 15.9; § 15.10 | Delaware law sits at our accepted fallback, but all Disputes go to ICDR international arbitration. Redlined at fallback level only: exclusive Delaware state and federal court jurisdiction, with ICDR applying only on later written agreement. § 7.5.5 expert determination and the injunctive-relief carve-out untouched. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15.11 (cf. § 15.10.2.4) | No cap and no carve-outs; direct liability uncapped both ways. Adding a mutual cap measured by twelve months of identified payments (SFJ's Development Costs; PB's Article 6 / § 14.2 payments), carving out indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | Development Costs (§ 4.2.3(ii)) | $110m minimum Elected Total Amount with no reduction mechanic and no true-up exit. Deleting the floor only; the $120m ceiling, election mechanic, overrun allocation and use-of-funds covenant untouched, as § 6.2 already pro-rates our Approval Payments. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Deviation | § 15.16 | Already mutual, solicitation-only, with an advertising carve-out, but runs for the Term plus a redacted tail and has no unsolicited-approach carve-out. Two surgical edits to the fallback: 12 months from the end of the employee's involvement, plus an unsolicited-approach carve-out. |
| Medium | TRANSITION | Missing | Term and Termination (§ 14.3; cf. § 10.3) | § 14.3 is conditional on a § 14.2 termination and no Program Transfer, so it does not apply on expiration; § 10.3 has no export deadline. Inserting fallback § 14.5: at least 90 days' assistance and data export within 30 days of any expiry or termination. |
| Medium | WARRANTY | Missing | Representations and Warranties (§ 13.5; § 13.6.2) | SFJ's performance is effectively "AS IS"; § 13.6.2 disclaims all warranties outside Article 13. Inserting new § 13.5.1: 30-day SFJ Services conformance and 90-day software-to-documentation conformance, with re-performance/repair/replacement or refund. |
| Medium | AUDIT | Compliant | Records (Art. 9; §§ 3.6, 3.18.2) | Better than preferred: SFJ has no audit or inspection right over PB. § 3.6 obligations are mutual or PB-controlled; § 3.18.2 is a reporting covenant. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | Security Interest (§ 7.5) | Meets preferred: no MFN, ROFR or matching obligation on PB. The "not less favorable" language is a lender subordination benchmark. |
| Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | Term and Termination (§ 14.1) | Meets preferred: finite Term ending on the last Approval Payment, no evergreen or renewal uplift. Absence of an express "renewal by mutual written agreement" statement is a wording point only. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | Indemnification and Insurance (§ 12.3) | Mutual programme in place, but E&O binds only professional-services subcontractors and there is no cyber/privacy cover; stated limits are redacted. Adding SFJ-level E&O of USD 1m and cyber/privacy of USD 2m in § 12.3.2, leaving the mutual structure and other limits untouched. |

---

## Walk-away items

These three sit at or across our walk-away line and should be treated as conditions of signing rather than negotiable trades:

1. **SFJ ownership of the Trial Data Package (§ 11.1.1.4).** Vesting the data and Research Results generated under our own Development Program in the counterparty, recoverable only by buy-back, is walk-away territory and gives SFJ rights far beyond processing to perform the services.
2. **The one-way IP indemnity (Art. 12).** No SFJ IP indemnity at all, combined with PB indemnifying infringement caused by "either Party", fails the fallback and sits at the walk-away line.
3. **SFJ's Change of Control termination right (§ 14.2.6).** A counterparty right to terminate in its sole discretion on a Change of Control of PB, with a 150% Development Costs payment, is expressly walk-away territory.

We would also treat the breach-triggered 300% Development Cost multiples under LD as close to that line; they fail both the preferred and fallback positions and are punitive in character.

---

## Next steps

1. **Hold the T4C redline.** The termination-for-convenience proposal failed verification and is flagged needs_review. We will re-draft against § 14.2.2 (including the orphaned credit cross-reference and the § 5.2.2.2 reference to § 14.2.10) and re-verify before it leaves our side.
2. **Confirm commercial mandate on the three walk-away items** with the business team, so we can state clearly in the cover note that data ownership, the reciprocal IP indemnity and deletion of § 14.2.6 are not trades.
3. **Ask for the redacted figures** we cannot price: the § 12.3 insurance limits, the § 14.2.2 notice period, the § 14.3.4(ii) trial-transfer period and the § 15.16 non-solicit tail. Several of our positions are calibrated to the fallback only because the numbers are unavailable.
4. **Circulate the verified redline** covering INDEMN, IP, ASSIGN, LD, GOVLAW, LOL-CAP, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT, TRANSITION, WARRANTY and INSURANCE, noting in the cover note that we are not marking up the nine compliant rules.
5. **Flag the preferred-level upgrades we did not press**, for use as give-and-take in negotiation: the USD 1m liability floor and data-protection/fraud/IP carve-outs under LOL-CAP; "perpetual/irrevocable" licence labelling; then-current rates, machine-readable format and deletion certification under TRANSITION; and the 12-month, workmanlike-standard warranty."}
